https://business-review.eu/lifestyle/art.text: Picasso en visite exhibition to open in Timișoara on September 17 A total of 69 works by Pablo Picasso from the collection of the Musée Picasso in Antibes will be shown in Timișoara as part of a special exhibition inaugurating Art Encounters’ new space. Tickets are now available online. Between September 17, 2026 and January 17, 2027, Art Encounters will present Picasso en visite, one of Romania’s major exhibitions this autumn, offering visitors an encounter with Pablo Picasso’s artistic universe through 69 works including paintings, drawings, engravings, lithographs, and ceramics from the collection of the Musée Picasso in Antibes. The exhibition takes as its starting point a distinctive period in the artist’s life and work. In 1946, Picasso was invited to work in the rooms of the Château Grimaldi, which at the time housed the region’s museum of history and archaeology. The artist had long dreamed of a place where he could work on a different scale from that allowed by his studio. The Mediterranean light, the sea, Greek mythology, and the atmosphere of southern France became deeply embedded in his imagination during a period of extraordinary creative freedom. The works shown in Timișoara invite visitors to discover this unique world. Tickets available online Tickets can be purchased online at bilete.artencounters.ro and through the Entertix platform. To give visitors sufficient time and space to engage with the works, while also ensuring their protection, access to the exhibition will be organised in timed slots with a limited number of visitors. Advance booking is recommended. Read more about Art Encounters to open new art centre in Timișoara with “Picasso en visite” exhibition read more Ticket prices: ● Adults aged 18–64: RON 65 (Tuesday–Thursday) / RON 75 (Friday–Sunday) ● Children aged 8–17: RON 20 / RON 25 ● Family ticket (2 adults + 2 children): RON 150 / RON 175 ● Seniors aged 65+ and students up to 26: RON 35 / RON 45 ● Private tour for two people: RON 500 Admission is free for children under eight accompanied by an adult, people with disabilities or reduced mobility and their companions, members of the press, and holders of AICA, ICOM, and ICOMOS cards, subject to prior booking at contact@artencounters.ro. One free-admission day per month On the last Tuesday of every month, the exhibition can be visited free of charge between 10:00 and 20:00. Tickets for these days will be available from the Art Encounters ticket office on the same morning, subject to availability. Guided tours Guided tours will be available in Romanian and selected foreign languages, subject to advance booking. Art Encounters will also organise free visits for school groups, with details about the programme and registration to be announced soon. Further information is available at artencounters.ro. PICASSO EN VISITE September 17, 2026 – January 17, 2027 Tuesday–Sunday | 10:00–20:00 Art Encounters | 46C Take Ionescu Blvd., Timișoara Information, tickets, and catalogue pre-orders: artencounters.ro The Art Encounters Foundation is supported by Banca Transilvania as strategic partner. The exhibition is also made possible with the support of Catena, exhibition partner, and Dedeman, education partner, alongside the Alber Foundation, which supports the educational programme dedicated to children and young people. Deloitte is the editorial partner, while the events programme is supported by Ploom and Conceptual Lab. The project also benefits from the support of ISHO and Bosch. https://www.dw.com/en/drone-sightings-br.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Mtf1 Drone sightings forced Luxembourg's only international airport to briefly suspend flights overnight [FILE: August 11, 2026] Image: Steven Mohr/SNS/picture alliance Advertisement Luxembourg authorities are investigating drone sightings that forced the country's main airport to temporarily suspend flights overnight, Prime Minister Luc Frieden said on Saturday. Frieden said Luxembourg was working with its NATO allies following the incident, which comes amid heightened European concern over suspected hybrid attacks linked to Russia . What happened at Luxembourg airport? National carrier Luxair said more than 1,800 passengers were affected, with 17 incoming flights diverted to airports including Brussels, Paris and Frankfurt . Flights resumed on Saturday, although Luxair warned that delays and knock-on disruption could continue. The airport said the closure was a precautionary measure to protect passengers, airline crews, airport employees and aircraft. Frieden stressed that it was too early to determine who was responsible. "We are analyzing the situation," Frieden told a televised press conference after an emergency meeting with the country's defense and interior ministers. Have other drones been spotted? Frieden said "potentially larger drones" had also been observed in Luxembourg's airspace in recent days. "This is new for Luxembourg, but it is not completely new for our neighboring countries," he said. "We will ensure, together with our partners, that we can guarantee the security of our populations," Frieden said. European governments have repeatedly warned of Russian-linked hybrid activities since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Such incidents have included suspected sabotage, cyberattacks and unauthorized drone flights. There is currently no evidence establishing who was responsible for the Luxembourg sightings.
